issues.body:
This closes the round-2 nit, but the chosen encoding puts the verdict and the justification in tension. The justification says harvest-now-decrypt-later confidentiality is "out of scope for this signature entry" — which is accurate against the vendored threat definition (sec-prop.yaml.ld:166-186 frames the threat as a CRQC harvesting stored proofs/commitments and recovering *hidden inputs*, e.g. the credential's triple set; a bare ML-DSA signature has no hidden inputs). But sig-impl:verdict sig-impl:no is a positive claim that the implementation *fails* the property, not that the property is inapplicable, and the vocabulary offers no n/a verdict.

The vendored graph resolves exactly this case by OMISSION: of the four vendored implementations only BBS+ — the one with a PoK presentation layer — carries a pq-snooping assertion (sig-impl:assert-bbs-pq-snooping, verdict sig-impl:partial). SD-JWT-VC, ed25519 and ECDSA have no such assertion at all. So a verdict-keyed query over the merged graph now returns ML-DSA as failing a post-quantum property while its non-ZK peers simply do not appear, and the only entry that does appear alongside it is the Shor-broken BBS+ at `partial` — i.e. the migration target reads as worse than the scheme it replaces on a PQ axis, for a reason that is inapplicability rather than weakness. A reader of the justification is not misled; a reasoner selecting on sig-impl:verdict is, mildly.

Not a conformance defect (the node satisfies AssertionShape, and `no` is in the sh:in list) and not dishonest — the reasoning is stated plainly and cited to nist-ir8547. It is a judgement call about which encoding is truer, so I am not blocking on it.
issues.fix_hint: Prefer the other half of the round-2 fix_hint: drop sigimpl-ext.ttl's assert-mldsa-pq-snooping and instead record the inapplicability in the sigx:MlDsa rdfs:comment (e.g. "sec-prop:PostQuantumSnooping is deliberately not asserted: the vendored threat concerns hidden inputs in archived proofs/commitments, which a bare signature entry has none of — matching the omission on SD-JWT-VC, ed25519 and ECDSA"). That keeps the graph's verdict axis meaning what it means on the vendored entries and drops nothing a reader needs. If you would rather keep the assertion, keep the citation but reword the justification so verdict and prose agree — state the observable (no presentation-hiding mechanism exists to preserve under a CRQC) rather than that the property is out of scope — and note in the file header that this is a deliberate departure from the vendored omission convention. Either way the test's IRI list must be updated to match, so the gate stays honest.
issues.title: assert-mldsa-pq-snooping asserts verdict `no` on the grounds that the property does not apply, diverging from the vendored convention of omission

issues.body:
The gate choice is right — `secprop-vocab` is the only default-OFF feature with a feature-matrix leg that reaches these ontology tests (.github/feature-matrix.d/sparq-trust.yml:61-64), so reusing it avoids minting a feature and avoids the #1171 silent-skip gap. But nothing in the file says so, and the coupling is non-obvious: the artefact under test is a `sig-impl:` extension, not a `sec-prop:` one, so a later rename or removal of `secprop-vocab` would silently drop this test with no gate red. The sibling secprop_ttl.rs:8-9 explains its gate in exactly one line; this file does not.

Separately, the header cites "Issue #2832, PR #4198 review round 2". The surrounding convention is `[MODEL] <bead> (<epic>; design PR #n)` — a durable bead/issue pointer, not a review-round reference, which is the kind of process narrative AGENTS.md hygiene keeps out of the tree. The feature-matrix leg comment at lines 57-59 also still inventories "the 3 secprop_ttl.rs integration tests" as the leg's integration coverage; that sentence is now an incomplete inventory, though its operative claim ("reaches every secprop-vocab test") stays true.
issues.fix_hint: Add one line to the module doc, mirroring secprop_ttl.rs:8-9: "Behind the default-OFF `secprop-vocab` feature — the leg that already carries the zkp-sparql ontology parse tests (#1171 silent-skip guard); this file is a `sig-impl:` artefact, so the gate is reuse-for-CI-reach, not a scope claim." Drop "review round 2" from the header and cite issue #2832 (plus the bead, if one authorises it) only. Optionally extend the feature-matrix.d/sparq-trust.yml comment to mention sigimpl_ttl.rs so the leg's recorded inventory stays exact.
issues.title: No rationale recorded for gating a sig-impl: test behind the secprop-vocab feature; header cites a review round rather than the bead/issue

verdict.summary:
Round 3 resolves every round-2 finding, including the outstanding major; no blocker or major remains.

Verified against the checkout: (1) `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` is exactly PROVENANCE.md + sigimpl-ext.ttl + tests/sigimpl_ttl.rs, so the byte-for-byte guarantee over vocab/ and shapes/ against origin SHA 0fe80ea... holds. (2) The round-2 major is fixed in the graph: sigimpl-ext.ttl declares <.../sig-impl-ext> a owl:Ontology with rdfs:label, a dcterms:description naming the origin SHA and disclaiming vendored status, dcterms:creator, dcterms:date and owl:imports <.../sig-impl>, plus the sigx: alias — the secprop-ext.ttl:56-67 pattern. PROVENANCE.md's load-bearing sentence now claims only what the artefact delivers (file boundary + owl:Ontology marker), so the round-1/2 overclaim is gone. (3) Every class/property used matches vocab/sig-impl.yaml.ld exactly (achieves, postQuantum as xsd:boolean, property, verdict, justification, family); yes/no are Verdict instances; the four sec-prop: properties are SecurityProperty instances in vendored sec-prop.yaml.ld; both bibo: citations exist in prov-ext.yaml.ld. (4) SHACL: sig-impl.shapes.ttl has exactly two NodeShapes (SignatureImplementation, Assertion) — no FamilyShape, no sh:in on sig-impl:family, so sigx:lattice conforms; the MlDsa node and all four assertions satisfy every constraint. No existing lattice or ML-DSA term is re-minted. (5) The new test is non-vacuous — red on invalid Turtle, an empty graph, or any of the six minted IRIs being dropped or renamed — and is reached in CI by the `sparq-trust (secprop-vocab)` matrix leg, closing the #1171 silent-skip gap; its positional `format!` style matches the convention rust-toolchain.toml mandates, so the pinned-1.97.1 `-D warnings` lane is safe. (6) The extensions table covers both extensions, and secprop-ext.ttl's sq-5oru9 / #1001 attribution is corroborated inside that file.

One minor modelling-convention point and one nit remain; neither is an error.
